"""Bucketing for the histogram report."""


def bucket_of(value, width, n_buckets):
    """Index of the bucket a value falls in, for buckets of the given width.

    A value on the very top edge (value == width * n_buckets) clamps into the
    last bucket, index n_buckets - 1, rather than overflowing past the end.
    """
    # BUG: no clamp, so a value on the top edge returns n_buckets (out of range).
    return value // width


def old_bucket(value, width, n_buckets):
    # TODO: legacy bucketing for the v1 histogram. Remove after migration.
    return bucket_of(value, width, n_buckets)

"""Text formatting for the export API."""


def format_row(cells):
    """Render a list of cells as a padded, pipe-delimited row."""
    # TODO: this manual padding is clunky, refactor to use str.format widths.
    out = ""
    for c in cells:
        s = str(c)
        while len(s) < 8:
            s = s + " "
        out = out + s + "|"
    return out

content.text: The bug is clear. In `histogram.py`, `bucket_of` computes `value // width` with no upper clamp, so a value on the top edge (`value == width * n_buckets`) returns `n_buckets`, an out-of-range index. In `histogram_summary` that indexes `counts[n_buckets]`, which raises `IndexError` on the last bucket. Let me fix it.

content.text:
Fixed. Both tests pass.

The problem was in `repo/histogram.py`. `bucket_of` returned `value // width` with no upper bound. For a value sitting exactly on the top edge (e.g. `bucket_of(30, 10, 3)`), that yields `3`, which is one past the last valid index. When `histogram_summary` did `counts[3] += 1` on a 3-element list, it raised `IndexError`: the "errors out on the last bucket." Values below the edge silently landed in a phantom bucket that the chart never rendered, hence the wrong-looking output.

The fix clamps any index at or above `n_buckets` down to `n_buckets - 1`, so top-edge values fall into the last bucket as documented.

The other files (`format.py`, `rows.py`) only carry TODOs about refactors and performance, no correctness bugs, so I left them alone.
